steps.title: Import React and createContext from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and createContext from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and createContext from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and createContext
import React, { createContext } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and createContext from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have React and createContext available for use in your file.
successCriteria: The import statement correctly imports React and createContext from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and createContext. This gives you the foundation to create a context for your cart.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and createContext from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and createContext from the 'react' package using an import statement.

steps.title: Import useState and useContext from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import the useState and useContext hooks from the 'react' package. Add this import statement below the existing React import.
steps.hint: Use the same import syntax as before, but specify useState and useContext instead of createContext.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing hooks from 'react'
import { useState, useContext } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have two import statements from 'react': one for React and createContext, and another for useState and useContext.
successCriteria: The import statement for useState and useContext is correctly added with proper syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported both useState and useContext hooks. These will be essential for managing state and consuming context in your cart functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both useState and useContext from 'react' using the correct import syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import both useState and useContext from the 'react' package using the same import syntax as the previous step.

steps.title: Define CartItem interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named CartItem with id (number), name (string), price (number), and quantity (number) properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a CartItem interface with typed properties that will represent items in the shopping cart.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the CartItem interface with all required properties and proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface is named 'CartItem' and includes all four properties with the correct TypeScript types: id (number), name (string), price (number), and quantity (number).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'CartItem', and define all four properties with TypeScript type annotations.

steps.title: Define CartContextType interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named CartContextType that describes the shape of your cart context. It should include a cart array of CartItem objects, an addItem function that takes a CartItem parameter and returns void, and a removeItem function that takes an item id (string) parameter and returns void.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name. Inside curly braces, define the properties: cart as CartItem[], addItem as a function type, and removeItem as a function type.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a CartContextType interface that defines the structure for your cart context, including the cart array and the add/remove functions.
successCriteria: The interface must be named CartContextType, include a cart property typed as CartItem[], an addItem function type, and a removeItem function type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! Your CartContextType interface correctly defines the shape of the cart context with the cart array and the add/remove functions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface includes all required properties: cart (CartItem[]), addItem function, and removeItem function.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look like a complete CartContextType interface. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and define all three required properties with proper TypeScript types.

steps.title: Create CartContext with createContext
steps.instruction: Create a context named CartContext using createContext. The context should have a type of CartContextType | undefined and be initialized with undefined.
steps.hint: Use the createContext function you imported earlier. Pass undefined as the initial value and specify the type using the CartContextType interface.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a context with a specific type
const ThemeContext = createContext<ThemeContextType | undefined>(undefined);
steps.expectedOutcome: A CartContext variable is created with the correct type and initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CartContext with the correct type and initial value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've used createContext with the CartContextType | undefined type and undefined initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CartContext wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use createContext with the CartContextType | undefined type and undefined as the initial value.

steps.title: Create CartProvider component
steps.instruction: Define a functional component named CartProvider that takes children as props. Use the CartContext created earlier.
steps.hint: Create a component that returns the CartContext.Provider. You'll need to pass children as a prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CartProvider component is defined with children prop and returns CartContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CartProvider component. This component will wrap your app and provide the cart context to all child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component is named CartProvider, accepts children as a prop, and returns CartContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CartProvider component is not defined correctly. Ensure you create a functional component named CartProvider that takes children as props and returns CartContext.Provider.

steps.title: Initialize cart state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'items' initialized as an empty array. The state should hold CartItem[] type items.
steps.hint: Use useState<CartItem[]>([]) to create the state. Remember to import useState if not already imported (it is in the code).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with useState
const [items, setItems] = useState<CartItem[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component now has a state variable 'items' initialized as an empty array, ready to hold cart items.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the cart state with useState. The 'items' state variable is now ready to store cart items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've used useState with the correct type (CartItem[]) and initialized it as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'items' of type CartItem[] initialized as an empty array.

steps.title: Define addToCart function
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, define a function named addToCart that takes a CartItem parameter and updates the cart state by adding the item.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setCart state setter to update the items array. You'll need to handle adding new items and updating quantities for existing items.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a function named addToCart that properly handles adding items to the cart state, including updating quantities for existing items.
successCriteria: Function updates cart state using setCart
Function handles both new items and existing items
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the addToCart function that properly manages adding items to the cart, including updating quantities for existing items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure your addToCart function properly handles both new items and existing items, and correctly updates the cart state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addToCart function is not defined correctly. Check that you've created a function with the right name and parameter, and that it properly updates the cart state.

steps.title: Define removeFromCart function
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, define a function named removeItem that takes an id parameter of type string and updates the cart state to remove the item with that id.
steps.hint: Use the setCart function to update the state. You can filter the current cart array to exclude items where the id matches the parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The removeItem function is defined inside CartProvider, taking a string id and updating the cart state by filtering out the matching item.
successCriteria: Filters cart array to remove matching id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the removeItem function that removes items from the cart by their id.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function: 1) is named removeItem, 2) takes an id parameter of type string, 3) uses setCart to update state, and 4) filters the cart array correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeItem function isn't defined correctly. Make sure to create a function that removes items from the cart state by filtering out items with a matching id.

steps.title: Create context value object
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, create a value object that contains the cart state and the addToCart and removeFromCart functions. This object should match the CartContextType interface.
steps.hint: Create a constant named value or contextValue that is an object with items, addItem, and removeItem properties. The items property should be the cart state, addItem should be the addToCart function, and removeItem should be the removeFromCart function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A value object is created inside CartProvider that contains the cart state and the two cart manipulation functions, ready to be provided to the context.
successCriteria: The code should contain an object (named value or contextValue) with properties items, addItem, and removeItem that reference the existing cart state and functions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the context value object that combines your cart state and functions. This object will be provided to the context consumers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your value object includes all three required properties: items, addItem, and removeItem. Also ensure they reference the correct variables (cart, addToCart, and removeFromCart).
steps.feedbackWrong: The context value object wasn't created correctly. Remember to create an object with items, addItem, and removeItem properties that reference your existing cart state and functions.

steps.title: Return CartContext.Provider with value
steps.instruction: Inside your CartProvider component, return CartContext.Provider with the value prop set to your context value object and children as its content.
steps.hint: Use the CartContext.Provider component and pass the value prop. The provider should wrap any children passed to CartProvider.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component now returns a CartContext.Provider that wraps its children and provides the context value.
successCriteria: value prop is set to the context value object
children are wrapped inside the provider
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the CartContext.Provider with the value prop, making the cart context available to all child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning CartContext.Provider with the value prop set to your context value object and children wrapped inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CartProvider component should return CartContext.Provider with the value prop and children. Check that you're using the correct context and passing the value properly.

steps.title: Export CartContext and CartProvider
steps.instruction: Export CartContext and CartProvider from the module so they can be imported and used in other components.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before the declarations or add export statements at the end of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: CartContext and CartProvider are exported and ready to be imported in other components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported CartContext and CartProvider. Now other components can import and use them.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported one of them, but both CartContext and CartProvider need to be exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure to export both CartContext and CartProvider using the export keyword.
